summary: A check that reports definitions present in a merge's second parent and absent from its result, wired into the existing rust.yml. The hard part was not counting but separating accident from intent, which is recorded as a per-commit trailer rather than a file so it cannot outlive the merge it excuses. The first design had a structural exemption for merges whose tree equals their first parent's; the mandated mutation test showed that exemption also swallowed the exact failure the check exists for, so it was removed in favour of an explicit wildcard trailer.
changes: scripts/check-merge-dropped-symbols.py: the check, with the intent trailer `Dropped-from-theirs: <name> -- <why>` and a `*` wildcard for merges that keep our tree on purpose. The file filter covers what the merged-in branch changed and what the merge changed; the trailer name is matched literally against the check's printed form
.github/workflows/rust.yml: a merge_drops job on the existing file (no new workflow), fetch-depth 0 because the check needs merge parents
CLAUDE.md: the DoD block gains the same command — the parity lock requires CI and DoD to match, and it now reports 7 commands on both sides
verification: PRECONDITION b, the gate that could have ended this ticket: reconstructed the loss on origin/main and ran every existing axis against it. Dropping a self-consistent slice (recipe_arity_call_site + RECIPE_ARITY + its write loop) leaves the generator at rc=0, audit-fixture-single-defect.py at rc=0 (23 checks), test_class_format 21 passed, test_fixture_pins 3 passed, check-dod-ci-parity rc=0, git status empty, zero conflict markers. Nothing catches it, so the gate does not fire

the same experiment with a NON-self-consistent slice does go red, but as an AttributeError crash rather than a diagnosis — which is why the silent case is the one that matters and had to be measured separately

PRECONDITION a, recount: the two resolutions e53b2142 and 514d5b08 each dropped 4 definitions, not the 3 the proposal states — LINKED, MAKECONCAT_DESCRIPTOR, def make_concat_call_site, method fieldref
MUTATION (a): a synthetic merge that discarded the other side's new function is rc=1 and names it — 'def kept_by_theirs — in the merged-in branch, not in the result'
NORMAL (b): the same merge resolved as a union is rc=0
INTENT (c): adding `Dropped-from-theirs: def kept_by_theirs -- superseded ...` makes it rc=0; removing the trailer returns it to rc=1; the `*` wildcard form is rc=0
SQUASH (d): a one-parent commit range reports '0 merge(s)' and rc=0

run against the real incident, the check reproduces by machine the same split the -fix3 round found by hand: 4 accidental drops in the generator plus 2 intentional test-function removals in tests/test_class_format.rs
cargo test --all: 583 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored, unchanged — no product code touched
check-dod-ci-parity: OK, 7 commands and 2 toolchains matching on both sides after the wiring

GATE 2 found the filter too narrow and this round widened it. The original looked only at files the merged-in branch changed, on the stated grounds that 'only files the merged-in branch actually changed can have lost its work' — which is false, and the repo's own second incident proves it: 514d5b08 dropped the same four definitions as e53b2142, and the narrow filter reported '0 file(s) examined', rc=0. The predicate is now every file that either the merged-in branch or the merge itself changed, and both incidents report rc=1 with the same six names.

The docstring's only worked example did not work. It wrote `Dropped-from-theirs: Pool.fieldref` while the check prints `method fieldref` and matches literally, so anyone following the example got no exemption. Verified both ways on a synthetic merge: the name copied from the output exempts (rc=0), the prettier form does not (rc=1). The example now uses the printed form and the docstring states that the name must be copied from the check's own output character for character.
issues: FALSE POSITIVE RATE, measured by this round by running both versions over one window of 83 merges (38b0df38..8c7b473f, the last 200 commits of origin/main at the time): the check as first written flags 8 merges / 19 definitions; the widened file filter flags 10 / 26. An earlier draft of this file said 45; that number was wrong and never came out of this implementation. The narrow version reproducing 19 exactly, in the same run, is what makes the measurement trustworthy. The seven extra definitions come from two merges, 514d5b08 (six) and 37ea5a13 (one), and they split four to three: four are the second of the two real incidents, restored later and present in the tree today; three are a branch having removed a definition main still had (two tests deleted on purpose by 0f517567, one predicate generalised by 1da1379e). So the honest rate is 4 of 7 found and 3 of 7 false, not 6 and 1. The widened version was no slower than the narrow one in that window, so time is not the cost of widening; reading is. A pull request usually contains 0-2 internal merges. CI only walks origin/main..HEAD, so historical merges are never re-examined and do not turn main red -- but that is not a reason to call the cost small, because the new cost lands in exactly that range, on the next base pull of an open branch.

WHAT IT CANNOT SEE: a definition whose name survives while its body is emptied or gutted. The check compares name sets, so 'still there but no longer does anything' passes. It also cannot tell a genuine rename from a drop-plus-add, and a move between files reads as a drop in the old file.

THE TRAILER IS A BYPASS, and deliberately so: anyone in a hurry can write one and move on. The only brake is that a reason is required by the format and the trailer is visible in the merge commit. That is weaker than a gate and stronger than nothing; making it harder was judged over-design for a check with no track record yet.

Two of the flagged historical merges are the known incident. The rest are upstream-sync merges (S5-S8) and one `-s ours` ancestry record. The sync ones genuinely dropped upstream methods — decode_str and encode_str are absent from the whole result tree, not moved, which was checked — so whether they are findings or accepted judgements is for the sync lineage to say, not this round.

The exemption name is matched literally against the check's own output, which is a sharp edge: `method fieldref` works and `Pool.fieldref` does not. The docstring now says so and its example uses the printed form, but nothing verifies a trailer's name is well-formed — a typo still reads as 'not exempted' rather than as 'you spelled it wrong'. There were 0 trailers anywhere in the repo's 1,286 commits when this changed, so nothing existing broke.
